item.title: Learning in Lost-Sales Inventory Systems with Stochastic Lead Times and Random Supplies
item.description:
Chen, X., Lyu, J., Yuan, S., Zhou, Y.
Supply uncertainty, characterized by stochastic lead times and random supply quantities, has attracted increasing attention from academia, industries, and governments, particularly in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic. In this paper, we consider the problem of managing lost-sales inventory systems with general supply uncertainty: stochastic lead times and random supplies. Unlike the previous studies, we assume the decision maker has no prior information on the stochastic demand and supply.

We examine the value of skilled immigrants in finance by exploiting evidence from visa lotteries. We find that hedge fund management companies that secure more H-1B visas in random lotteries deliver higher alphas, Sharpe ratios, and information ratios. The superior performance of funds with high H-1B visa allocations can be attributed to well-paid and highly educated H-1B workers with quantitative skills. Traders devote significant resources to producing private information. The value of such information is eroded when it is leaked. We study the use of multiple brokers by institutions to help mitigate information leakage. item.description:

This paper investigates how environmental regulatory uncertainty affects green innovation in polluting firms. The findings suggest that, instead of adopting a passive “wait-and-see” strategy, polluting firms proactively engage in green innovation and R&D activities. item.description:

Do job seekers consider the race or gender of an employer when applying for a job? Although we have extensive research on employer-side discrimination, we know less about employee-side biases and their consequences. In this study, we examine how the gender and race of the employer shape the willingness of prospective employees to apply for a job. We study a newsvendor problem with unknown demand distribution in a nonstationary demand environment over a multiperiod time horizon. The demand in each period consists of a time-varying demand level and an additive random shock. Neither the demand level nor the random shock is separately observable. item.title: Incident Zero by Abdullah Rehman: A First-Day Challenge for AP® Cybersecurity
item.description:
Abdullah Rehman
Incident Zero is a first-day or second-day collaborative cybersecurity investigation designed for AP Cybersecurity classrooms. Students work in teams to analyze five short evidence-based security challenges involving risk, physical security, networks, devices, and data. Each investigation produces an unlock letter, leading students to the final recovery word and introducing the concept of defense in depth. The activity is intentionally designed for students with no prior cybersecurity knowledge.

Over the past 25 years, the Traveling Tournament Problem (TTP) has become one of the most extensively studied optimization problems in sports scheduling.
